A 1099-NEC goes to GA DOR with the G-1003 only if Georgia tax was withheld (2026 Employer's Tax Guide p.7, 20), so a founder who withheld nothing has no GA filing for contractors.

question: We'll have 12 full-timers on Jan 1, plus a couple of part-timers. Our City of Roswell business license renews in the spring. Someone mentioned E-Verify. Is that required for us now?

must_include.fact: Georgia requires E-Verify for private employers with more than 10 employees, counting only those working 35+ hours a week as of January 1
You give your E-Verify number with each business license application or renewal (at 10 or fewer you sign the exemption affidavit)
Legal basis is O.C.G.A. § 36-60-6
Roswell certificates expire Dec 31 and the tax is due March 15, with a 10% penalty if not renewed by then

notes: Primary: headcount-triggers-and-compliance-calendar. Multi-package (headcount + local licenses + checklist). Good answer: yes, 12 full-time on Jan 1 is over 10; enroll at e-verify.gov (founder's portal) before the renewal; Roswell counts W-2 employees working 35+ hours; part-timers don't count under state law but local forms can differ.

question: I've got the GA DOL Employer Handbook (DOL-224) open. What's the minimum salary I can pay my first developer and still not owe overtime? And is there a pay level where they're automatically exempt?

must_include.fact: The salary level for exemption is at least $684/week ($35,568/year)
A computer employee paid hourly can be exempt at $27.63/hour or more
Highly compensated employee: $107,432 or more total annual comp (including at least $684/week salary) AND regularly performs one exempt duty; no pay level is automatic
The 2024 rule ($844 / $1,128) was vacated; DOL restored the 2019 text on May 15, 2026

must_not_say.trap: Quotes the outdated $455/week salary threshold or $100K HCE threshold from dol224.pdf as current
Treats the vacated 2024 rule thresholds ($844 / $1,128 per week) as current

notes: Primary: exempt-vs-nonexempt-pay-rules. Trap: $455/week and $100K HCE from dol224.pdf. A great answer may mention that the handbook figures are outdated (allowed) but must not present them as current. It should say the duties test still applies; there is no automatic pay level.

question: Can I pay my first dev only in equity? She's cool with it: 2% of the company, no cash until we raise in about 6 months, then we'd backpay her salary.

must_include.fact: Equity isn't wages: minimum wage and overtime must be paid in cash or negotiable instrument payable at par (29 CFR 531.27); options don't count toward $7.25
Equity can't make up the $684/week salary needed for exemption
Unpaid back wages bring liquidated damages equal to the unpaid amount; claims reach back 2 years (3 if willful)
The 20% owner exemption covers founders who own at least 20% and actively manage; it doesn't extend to a first hire with 2%

must_not_say.trap: Says equity can replace or count toward minimum wage/salary

notes: Primary: exempt-vs-nonexempt-pay-rules. Multi-package (pay rules + equity + founders). Should-refer: employment attorney for 'equity instead of pay' and accrued salary. Founders can be personally liable (29 U.S.C. § 203(d)); deferral can trigger 409A. Safe pattern: legal minimum in cash, equity on top.

question: We want a Georgia Tech student as an unpaid summer intern who'd ship real features. The GA DOL handbook has an intern test we were going to use. Also, can we just run payroll monthly to keep things simple?

must_include.fact: Use DOL Fact Sheet #71 (Jan 2018): an intern can be unpaid only if the intern is the primary beneficiary, judged on 7 factors
An intern who ships production code is an employee: pay at least $7.25/hour plus overtime
Georgia requires pay dates that split the month into at least two equal periods (semimonthly); don't pay a developer monthly

must_not_say.trap: Uses the outdated six-factor intern test printed in dol224.pdf (current guidance is the FS71 seven-factor primary-beneficiary test)
Says monthly payroll is fine for a developer in Georgia

notes: Primary: exempt-vs-nonexempt-pay-rules. Trap: the handbook's outdated six-factor intern test. Good answer: shipping features means paid; if they insist on unpaid, document all 7 FS71 factors with the school beforehand and talk to an employment attorney; run payroll semimonthly, biweekly, or weekly.

question: We're 6 people on a basic payroll service. A PEO is pitching us: better health plans, and they say they'd 'take on the liability.' Is that true? And if we leave them in 2 years, what happens with Georgia unemployment?

must_include.fact: Only an IRS-certified PEO (CPEO) is solely liable for federal employment taxes, and only for wages it pays; with a non-certified PEO you generally keep the liability
Check certification on the IRS CPEO public listings, updated quarterly
A GA PEO reports UI under its own GA DOL account; if it hasn't posted the bond, the client is liable and it reports under the client's account
The Georgia PEO bond is the greater of $10,000 or 2.7% of taxable payroll

must_not_say.trap: Says any PEO takes over all of the company's tax liability
States as fact the GA UI rate you'll get after leaving a PEO (the package marks this an unverified inference)

notes: Primary: payroll-peo-and-benefits. Good answer: verify CPEO status and EIN in the contract, ask the vendor questions list, note that on exit you file DOL-4N under your own account and the rate and wage-base restart aren't verified, and suggest a CPA and an employment attorney to review the PEO contract.

question: We're 3 people including me. Do I legally have to offer health insurance? I keep hearing about QSEHRAs. What's the deal? And does Georgia make us give paid sick days?

must_include.fact: No federal mandate to offer health coverage under 50 full-time employees plus FTEs (ACA employer mandate starts at 50)
QSEHRA 2026 caps are $6,450 self-only and $13,100 family; you must have under 50 FT+FTE and offer no group plan
QSEHRA/ICHRA written notice is due 90 days before the plan year
Georgia doesn't require private employers to give paid vacation or sick leave, and local mandates are preempted

must_not_say.trap: Says Georgia requires paid sick leave

notes: Primary: payroll-peo-and-benefits. Good answer: no requirement; QSEHRA or ICHRA as low-admin options; kin care only at 25+ employees and only if you offer sick leave; small business health credit needs SHOP coverage; benefits broker for choices.

question: I need to fire my only employee. Performance has been bad for months. Georgia is at-will, right? I found a Georgia 'At-Will Employment' PDF from the State Accounting Office and was going to cite it in the termination letter as the law. What else do I owe her?

must_include.fact: Georgia's at-will rule is O.C.G.A. § 34-7-1: an indefinite hiring may be terminated at will by either party
Give the Separation Notice (DOL-800) on the last day of work, or send it within 3 days by email or mail if she's unavailable
Answer a UI claim (DOL-1199FF) within 10 calendar days or by the date on the notice
Appeal a UI determination within 15 days

must_not_say.trap: Treats the GA State Accounting Office at-will PDF as Georgia law (it's SAO policy for state employees; the at-will rule is O.C.G.A. § 34-7-1)

notes: Primary: firing-and-offboarding-ga. Trap: treating the SAO at-will PDF as Georgia law (it's SAO policy for state employees; ANSWERING_GUIDE says don't). Good answer: cite § 34-7-1, document the performance issue (for UI, 'inability by itself is not misconduct', so she may still get benefits), final pay on the next regular payday, PTO per policy, revoke access, I-9 retention; employment attorney if she's in a protected class or recently complained.

question: We're 22 people. We're laying off a 52-year-old engineer (role eliminated). We want to give 6 weeks of severance in exchange for a release, with a strict confidentiality and non-disparagement clause and a 3-year non-compete. What do we need to know?

must_include.fact: OWBPA: a release from someone 40+ must give 21 days to consider (45 in a group program) and 7 days to revoke
The ADEA (and OWBPA) applies at 20+ employees
Under NLRB McLaren Macomb (2023), still Board law as of 2026-10-25, broad confidentiality and non-disparagement clauses offered to non-supervisors violate the NLRA
Georgia presumes a restrictive covenant of 2 years or less reasonable; non-competes bind only certain roles (sales, managers, key employees)

must_not_say.trap: Says the FTC non-compete ban is in effect

notes: Primary: firing-and-offboarding-ga. Should-refer: severance for someone 40+ goes to an employment attorney. Good answer: OWBPA plain-language, names the ADEA, advise counsel, no bar on EEOC charges; a 3-year non-compete exceeds the 2-year presumption and may not reach a non-key engineer; narrow the clauses; list severance on the DOL-800; at 22 employees COBRA applies.

question: I run my startup from my house. My mailing address says Decatur but I think I'm actually in unincorporated DeKalb. Zero revenue so far. Do I really need a business license? What's it going to cost?

must_include.fact: DeKalb charges a $75 administrative fee and a $50 minimum tax even at $0 receipts
DeKalb renewals: file by Feb 1, pay by Apr 15 (2026)
DeKalb late filing penalties: $100 after Feb 1, $300 after Mar 1, $600 after Apr 1
Sign the E-Verify exemption affidavit (10 or fewer employees) with the application

must_not_say.trap: Says a pre-revenue business doesn't need a license

notes: Primary: local-business-licenses-metro-atlanta. Good answer: check the physical address (not mailing city) in the county lookup; if unincorporated DeKalb, file the Home-Based Business Application on epermits.dekalbcountyga.gov, clear zoning, sign E-Verify and SAVE affidavits (often notarized). If it's actually in the City of Decatur, Decatur's figures are unverified, so confirm with the city.

question: We just signed a lease for an office in Gwinnett, Peachtree Corners area, though I'm not sure if that's a city or unincorporated. We have 7 employees. When do business license renewals hit, and what happens if we're late?

must_include.fact: A city taxes businesses within its corporate limits; the county taxes only unincorporated areas, so check the address, not the mailing city
Peachtree Corners is an incorporated city, so an office inside its limits files with the city (Finance Department), not Gwinnett County
Peachtree Corners: renew annually; a penalty applies if you don't file by Mar 31 when you operated the prior year (current renewal date not posted, so confirm)
Peachtree Corners late penalties: 10% of the amount owed per calendar year, plus 1.5% per month interest
must_include.row: LOCAL_BUSINESS_LICENSES_METRO_ATLANTA: Peachtree Corners penalties and fees

must_not_say.trap: Says Peachtree Corners is unincorporated Gwinnett, or that Gwinnett County's license rules govern an address inside the city

notes: Primary: local-business-licenses-metro-atlanta. Peachtree Corners is an incorporated city in Gwinnett with its own OTC (row added 2026-10-26). Good answer: confirm the address is inside city limits, then give the city's rules: annual renewal through BS&A Online, penalty if not filed by Mar 31, 10% per calendar year plus 1.5%/month interest, 30-day rule for new businesses, and a Zoning Use Approval before applying. Gwinnett County's Feb 15 / $25 / 10% rules apply only if the address turns out to be unincorporated. The current renewal due date isn't posted (2022 form said Mar 31), so tell them to confirm with the city. At 7 employees they sign the E-Verify exemption affidavit.

question: We're a Delaware C-corp, but the company, both founders, and all 5 employees are in San Francisco. Nothing in Georgia. What's California's final paycheck deadline when we fire someone, and do we have to give paid sick leave?

must_include.fact: These packages only cover US federal plus Georgia law; California employment law is outside the scope
must_include.row: ANSWERING_GUIDE: Scope (Jurisdiction: US federal plus Georgia; no double-check row)

must_include.fact: Send state-specific questions to an employment attorney licensed in the work state
must_include.row: REMOTE_AND_OUT_OF_STATE_HIRES: When to bring in a professional (employment attorney licensed in the work state)

question: Totally unrelated to the company: my wife and I are trying to decide whether to file jointly or separately this year, and whether we can claim our daughter's daycare. What would you do?

must_include.fact: Personal income tax filing is outside the scope of these packages (startup hiring and running a business in GA)
Refer to a CPA or tax preparer

question: We sell B2B SaaS subscriptions, and a bunch of our customers are in Georgia. Do we need to charge Georgia sales tax on them?

must_include.fact: GA sales and use tax on SaaS isn't covered by any package; it's an open item in the question bank ('verify; this varies')
must_include.row: QUESTION_BANK: Taxes (GA sales and use tax on SaaS; not yet a package)

must_include.fact: Send it to a CPA or the Georgia Department of Revenue

Confuses the local occupation tax with sales tax
